```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
pacman::p_load(sf, spatstat, sparr, terra, tmap, tidyverse)

study_area <- st_read("data/raw", layer = "gadm41_IDN_2", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  filter(NAME_2 == "Pulang Pisau") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32749)

fire_archive <- read_csv("data/raw/fire_archive_J1V-C2_811410.csv",
                         col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
fire_nrt     <- read_csv("data/raw/fire_nrt_J1V-C2_811410.csv",
                         col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
fire_raw <- bind_rows(archive = fire_archive, nrt = fire_nrt, .id = "source") %>%
  type_convert()

fire_clean <- fire_raw %>%
  distinct() %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
         between(latitude, -90, 90), between(longitude, -180, 180)) %>%
  filter(confidence %in% c("n", "h")) %>%
  mutate(acq_date = as.Date(acq_date)) %>%
  filter(acq_date >= as.Date("2026-01-01"), acq_date <= as.Date("2026-09-23")) %>%
  mutate(Month_num = month(acq_date))

fire_sf <- fire_clean %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32749) %>%
  st_intersection(study_area)

fire_dedup <- fire_sf %>%
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  distinct(x, y, acq_date, .keep_all = TRUE)

fire_owin <- as.owin(study_area)
fire_ppp  <- as.ppp(st_geometry(fire_dedup)); Window(fire_ppp) <- fire_owin
fire_ppp  <- rjitter(fire_ppp, retry = TRUE, nsim = 1, drop = TRUE)
fire_ppp.km <- rescale.ppp(fire_ppp, 1000, "km")

kde_ppl <- density(fire_ppp.km, sigma = bw.ppl, edge = TRUE, kernel = "gaussian")

fire_month <- fire_dedup %>% select(Month_num)
fire_month_ppp  <- as.ppp(fire_month)
fire_month_owin <- fire_month_ppp[fire_owin]
st_kde <- spattemp.density(fire_month_owin, lambda = 1.5)
```

#  {.title-slide background-color="#3c6e47"}

::: title-block
### Forest-fire Point Patterns {.r-fit-text}

#### Kabupaten Pulang Pisau, Central Kalimantan · 2026

Take-home Exercise 1 — Executive Summary\
**Meng Xinyu** · ISSS626 Geospatial Analytics
:::

## Research question & study area {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
Peatland fires in Central Kalimantan cause haze, health and economic harm. This study asks two questions of the 2026 satellite record:

-   **Q1** — Where does fire-detection intensity concentrate, and when?
-   **Q2** — Are detections significantly clustered, beyond just being dense?

Study window: **Kabupaten Pulang Pisau**, a peat-dominated regency.
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
```{r}
#| fig-height: 4
tm_shape(study_area) + tm_polygons(col = "#cfe3d4", border.col = "#3c6e47") +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE)
```
:::
:::::

## Data & study design {.smaller}

|  |  |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Detections** | NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20), 1 Jan – 23 Sep 2026 |
| **Boundary** | GADM ADM2 (regency), UTM 49S (EPSG:32749) |
| **Point event** | one detection ≠ one fire → de-duplicated to one point per pixel per day |
| **Cleaning** | 370,354 → 351,822 national → **16,189** inside the regency |

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
A detection is not a distinct fire — repeated overpasses inflate apparent clustering, so de-duplication comes first.
:::

## Analytical approach {.smaller}

Following the class workflow (r4gdsa Ch. 4–6):

| Question            | Method                          | Compared against   |
|---------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------|
| Is it random?       | **Clark-Evans test**            | CSR (Monte Carlo)  |
| Where is intensity? | **Kernel density (KDE)**        | —                  |
| Do points interact? | **G / F / K / L functions**     | homogeneous CSR    |
| Robustness          | **Inhomogeneous L**             | inhomogeneous null |
| Timing              | **Spatio-temporal KDE** (sparr) | —                  |

## First-order — intensity concentrates in the south {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.6
kde_terra <- rast(kde_ppl); crs(kde_terra) <- "EPSG:32749"
tm_shape(kde_terra) +
  tm_raster(palette = "YlOrRd", title = "Intensity") +
  tm_shape(study_area) + tm_borders(col = "grey30") +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, legend.outside = TRUE)
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
**Clark-Evans R = 0.42** (p = 0.01) → clustered, not random.

The KDE hotspot sits in the **central-south peatland**, and is stable across all three bandwidths — the peak location does not depend on the smoothing choice.
:::
:::::

## Second-order — strong clustering vs CSR {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](Take-home_Ex01_files/figure-html/lest-1.png)
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
The observed **L-curve sits far above** the CSR envelope across all scales up to \~20 km.

**G, F, K and L all agree**: the detections are significantly more clustered than a random pattern — the signature of fires concentrated in a few active areas.
:::
:::::

## Value-added 1 — is the clustering real? {.smaller}

The CSR test assumes constant intensity, which is false here. The **inhomogeneous L** lets intensity vary and re-tests.

::: fragment
-   Under a **homogeneous** null → detections look strongly clustered.
-   Once **intensity is allowed to vary** → the curve drops back near the baseline.
:::

::: {.fragment .callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
**Key result:** the clustering mostly reflects **first-order heterogeneity** — fires concentrate because the *conditions* for fire concentrate — not extra fire-to-fire interaction.
:::

## Value-added 2 — activity builds up in time {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.6
tims <- c(6, 7, 8, 9)
par(mfcol = c(2, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1))
for (i in tims) {
  plot(st_kde, i, override.par = FALSE, fix.range = TRUE,
       main = paste("Month", i))
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
The spatio-temporal KDE shows the hotspot **stays in the central-south peatland** but **grows stronger** as the dry season advances.

So **timing matters as much as location** — the same core is at risk, but the risk window concentrates in a few months.
:::
:::::

## Key findings {.smaller}

-   **First-order** — Clark-Evans confirms clustering; intensity concentrates in the central-south peatland.
-   **Second-order** — G/F/K/L all show significant clustering vs CSR…
-   **…but** the **inhomogeneous L** shows it is *mostly first-order heterogeneity*, not fire-to-fire interaction.
-   **Timing** — activity peaks in the dry-season months.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
First- and second-order evidence agree: a few peat-dominated areas drive the whole pattern.
:::

## Limitations & implications {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Read with care**

-   Detections ≠ fires; cloud/overpass gaps.
-   Concentration ≠ risk without exposure data.
-   CSR/KDE assumptions only partly hold.
-   Window stops in September.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**From evidence to action**

-   **Where** — focus monitoring & patrols on the central-south peatland.
-   **When** — raise readiness ahead of the dry-season peak.
-   **Longer term** — peatland water management (levels, canal blocking).
:::
:::::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal"}
Directly supported: **spatial concentration + timing**. Needs more data: causation, who is exposed.
:::
